faq.q: How long does it take to make a wedding slideshow?
faq.a: Plan on roughly 6 to 7 hours over a few evenings for a 7-minute show. Here’s the rough math: about 2 hours gathering photos, 40 minutes scanning 80 prints at 30 seconds each, an hour choosing, 2 to 3 hours building and timing, and 30 minutes for a test run. Scanning and choosing grow fastest with a big family archive, so start those first.

faq.q: Can I make a wedding slideshow on my phone?
faq.a: Yes. On an iPhone, iMovie is free and its Magic Movie feature builds a first draft you can edit, and CapCut runs on iPhone and Android. As of November 2026, the iPhone Photos app can also play an album as a slideshow with your choice of song, time per slide and looping, and AirPlay it to a TV. For a long, carefully timed show, a computer is still easier.

faq.q: What is the best free wedding slideshow maker?
faq.a: On a Mac, iPhone or iPad, use iMovie: it’s free, handles titles and music well and exports in HD. On Windows or a Chromebook, start with Canva’s or CapCut’s free plan, and check that the template you like isn’t marked as a paid one. For a slideshow that only loops in the background, an Apple Photos slideshow or a Google Photos highlight video is the fastest option.

faq.q: Should a wedding slideshow have music if we have a DJ?
faq.a: For a sit-down showing, yes: ask the DJ to fade the room music, then play the slideshow’s sound through their system. For a slideshow that loops during cocktail hour or dinner, WeddingWire’s slideshow guide suggests leaving it music-free so the DJ or band can set the mood. Tell your DJ either way so they can plan the handoff.

faq.q: Who should run the slideshow at the reception?
faq.a: One person who isn’t you: usually the DJ, the venue’s AV contact or a friend who is comfortable with laptops. Give them the file on a USB drive, a cloud link, the exact cue (for example, right after the toasts) and the coordinator’s number. Ask them to do the test run with you, on the same laptop.

faq.q: How do we share the slideshow with guests after the wedding?
faq.a: Send a link in your thank-you texts or post it on your wedding website. If the slideshow uses commercial songs, expect copyright claims on public video platforms, so a version with royalty-free music is safer to upload. For Instagram or TikTok, a short vertical cut of 15 to 60 seconds usually works better than the full room version.
